subject: Money
title: Meme Stocks
description: A quick, practical guide to Meme Stocks.

hook.text: In January 2021, a Reddit forum turned GameStop into a $80 billion company. Hedge funds lost $6 billion in days.

buildup.text: WallStreetBets identified heavily shorted stocks and coordinated mass buying. A short squeeze sent prices vertical.

discovery.text: Social media replaced institutional research. Memes became investment theses. Irony became market strategy.

twist.text: Robinhood halted buying, protecting hedge funds. Retail investors felt the system was rigged against them.

climax.text: Meme stocks showed retail power but also its limits. Most holders who bought the top lost money.

punchline.text: The internet beat Wall Street. Briefly.

quiz.question: What made GameStop's stock surge in January 2021?
options: A coordinated short squeeze by retail investors
